To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the ortho-H218 O 110 → 100 line was not detected at the level of a 5 σ upper limit of 0.05 K, (ii) the ortho-to-para H2O abundance ratio in Orion is 2-3, (iii) the average ortho-H2 O abundance is 3-4 × 10- 8, and (iv) the ortho H2 O abundance is relatively constant over the region mapped.

(1) the H2O line is extended over 20'; (2) the line width and VLSR velocity are consistent with an origin from cold gas in the molecular ridge; (3) the ortho-H216O abundance is 3 × 1010 relative to H2; and (4) the ortho-to-para ratio is less than 1.5.
(a) water emission is widespread in Orion and (b) the ortho-H 2O/H2 abundance is approximately 3 × 108 in the extended gas of the cloud.

the detection and characterization of water vapor in the Orion molecular clouds.
the formation of water in the interstellar medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the water abundance in the extended cold gas in Orion is in the range (1-8) × 10-7 relative to H2, with an average value of 3 ×10-8.
the water abundance in Orion is not enhanced, and the water abundance in dense gas is not enhanced.
water is a common constituent of the cold, dense gas in the Orion molecular ridge, with a mean abundance of 2 × 10-9 relative to H2, and that the ortho-to-para ratio is near the expected value of 3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the water vapor abundance relative to H 2 in the cold gas in Orion is 3 × 107, which is about an order of magnitude larger than the cosmic abundance.
the water abundance in the extended gas is similar to that of the Orion Bar and that the ortho-to-para ratio is similar to the high-temperature equilibrium ratio of 3.
we have observed a large amount of water in Orion, with a wide range of velocities, but with a relatively low abundance relative to H218O.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ortho-water abundance is not enhanced by a factor of a few in the extended gas of Orion.
the ortho-to-para ratio of H2O is very high in the extended gas of Orion, and that the H2O is not in chemical equilibrium.
the ortho-to-para H2O abundance ratio is not significantly different from unity in the extended gas of Orion.
